title: Protesters interrupt War Secretary Pete Hegseth at Army event in Washington

tea.why: Protesters opposed military actions and defense spending during an Army conference panel featuring War Secretary Pete Hegseth.
tea.want: Protesters called out war policies, the conflict involving Iran, and civilian casualties in Gaza.
tea.changed: Oct 14: At least six anti-war demonstrators interrupted War Secretary Pete Hegseth during his remarks at an Army conference in Washington, D.C.

summary: On October 14, 2026, at least six anti-war demonstrators repeatedly interrupted War Secretary Pete Hegseth during a panel appearance at the Association of the United States Army conference in Washington, D.C. The protesters shouted slogans condemning the administration's military policies, calling the secretary a war criminal, a Nazi, and a coward, while raising issues regarding civilian casualties in Gaza and military spending. Event authorities and security personnel escorted the demonstrators out of the conference room, with one uncooperative protester being carried out by her arms and legs. Hegseth and other panelists on stage characterized the disruptions as a coordinated effort to delegitimize their remarks.
demands: Redirect military spending to domestic needs
response: Security personnel and authorities escorted at least six protesters out of the conference room, with one uncooperative individual carried out by her arms and legs. Secretary Hegseth and fellow panelists described the disruptions as a semi-coordinated effort.

updates.text: At least six protesters interrupted War Secretary Pete Hegseth multiple times at an Army conference in Washington, D.C., and were escorted out.
